title: How well behaved is finite dimensional Diffusion Maps embedding?
claim: A theoretical guarantee is built from assumptions and data through ordered parameter choices and computations to a final estimate.
layout: 2 merging columns flowing top-to-bottom, math-filled boxes, rounded input boxes
description: A black-and-white flowchart of boxes connected by downward arrows. Two parallel columns start at the top with rounded input boxes. The left box lists manifold-family assumptions: dimension, reach, Ricci curvature, volume and smoothness. The right box gives data points with uniform density. The left column goes through two boxes that control the injectivity radius and diameter, then compute the diffusion time t, the error epsilon-prime and the eigenvalue count m. The right column computes the bandwidth h and then constructs the matrices W, D and L_n. Diagonal arrows merge the two columns into a box that computes the first m eigenvalues and eigenvectors of L_n. A single column continues to the diffusion-maps embedding formula and ends in a rounded box that estimates tangent spaces at the embedded points. The boxes are dense with equations, and the eye starts at the large top-left assumptions box.
caption: Flowchart
abstract: Under a set of assumptions on a family of submanifolds $\subset {\mathbb R}^D$, we derive a series of geometric properties that remain valid after finite-dimensional and almost isometric Diffusion Maps (DM), including almost uniform density, finite polynomial approximation and reach. Leveraging these properties, we establish rigorous bounds on the embedding errors introduced by the DM algorithm is $O\left((\frac{\log n}{n})^{\frac{1}{8d+16}}\right)$. Furthermore, we quantify the error between the estimated tangent spaces and the true tangent spaces over the submanifolds after the DM embedding, $\sup_{P\in \mathcal{P}}\mathbb{E}_{P^{\otimes \tilde{n}}} \max_{1\leq j \angle (T_{Y_{Ï(M),j}}Ï(M),\hat{T}_j)\leq \tilde{n}} \leq C \left(\frac{\log n }{n}\right)^\frac{k-1}{(8d+16)k}$, which providing a precise characterization of the geometric accuracy of the embeddings. These results offer a solid theoretical foundation for understanding the performance and reliability of DM in practical applications.
